title: registry: re-registering a package whose new manifest no longer extends an object keeps the old extension's fields served
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgVLY5efsfaT3UG2zwH

## What happens

When a package is registered again (rebuild, reload, re-install of the same id) and its new manifest no longer carries an `objectExtensions` entry for an object the previous registration extended, the previous extension stays registered. Its fields keep being served on the target object.

The extend branch of object registration replaces a package's previous contribution to a target only when the new registration names that same target (`packages/objectql/src/registry-object-registration.ts`, around line 596: "extend mode: remove existing extension from same package"). Nothing withdraws a target the new registration does not name.

Found while measuring #35228 (decision analysis comment 7016526323, premise 4).

## Measured on main e35cf035 (bare registrar, vitest, `packages/objectql`)

```ts
const e = new ObjectQL();
e.registerApp({ id: 'com.t.core', name: 'core', version: '1.0.0', type: 'app', namespace: 'crm',
  objects: [{ name: 'crm_line', label: 'Line', fields: { name: { name: 'name', type: 'text', label: 'Name' } } }] });
e.registerApp({ id: 'com.t.mod', name: 'mod', version: '1.0.0', type: 'module',
  objectExtensions: [{ extend: 'crm_line', fields: { cb_account: { name: 'cb_account', type: 'text', label: 'A' } } }] });
e.registerApp({ id: 'com.t.mod', name: 'mod', version: '1.0.1', type: 'module', objectExtensions: [] });
// → crm_line still serves cb_account
```

Renaming the field in the second registration (same target) does replace it correctly: `cb_account2` is served and `cb_account` is gone.

## Measure first (before any fix)

This was measured on the bare `registerApp` only. Before treating it as a defect, check which real paths re-register a package without uninstalling it first, and whether any of them reaches this state:

1. `os dev` / source reload after an author deletes an extension entry.
2. A package upgrade (new version of an installed package that drops an extension), including the upgrade plan's view of removed fields (#34095).
3. A re-install of the same id through install-local.

For each, record whether the removed extension's fields are still served, and whether schema sync, the upgrade plan or the served object say anything about it. If every real path uninstalls first, record that and close this as not reachable.

## Expected

After a package is registered again, the served object carries exactly the extensions the package's current manifest declares.
